summary: MISSION CONTROL is an interactive educational game that lets players experience the challenges of designing and managing a space mission. Players select a mission to Earth, the Moon, Mars, or deep space, build a spacecraft by choosing scientific instruments and essential systems, and balance mass, power, and budget constraints. They then select a launch vehicle and orbit before launching and monitoring their mission through a simulation. Each decision influences mission performance and the final outcome. By turning complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible interactive experience, MISSION CONTROL encourages experimentation, problem-solving, and interest in space exploration.
details:
Project Details — MISSION CONTROL

What We Developed

MISSION CONTROL is an interactive space mission design and management simulator developed to make aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand through gameplay.

The player takes the role of a mission designer and makes decisions throughout the lifecycle of a space mission, from initial planning to mission completion.

How It Works

The game offers four mission categories: Earth Observation, Lunar Exploration, Mars Exploration, and Deep Space Exploration.

Players select a mission and build a spacecraft by choosing components such as solar panels, batteries, communication antennas, onboard computers, cameras, radar systems, and spectrometers.

Each component influences spacecraft characteristics such as mass, cost, power requirements, and mission capabilities. Players must balance these factors while staying within the available budget.

After spacecraft design, players select a launch vehicle and a suitable orbit or trajectory. They then complete pre-launch checks, launch the mission, and monitor its progress through a Mission Control interface.

The simulation tracks mission resources and performance, including energy, communications, scientific data, and mission progress. At the end, players receive a mission report evaluating the outcome of their decisions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Space mission design involves complex engineering concepts that can be difficult for beginners to understand. MISSION CONTROL makes these concepts more accessible by allowing players to experiment with different spacecraft configurations and observe the consequences of their choices.

The project aims to:

  • Encourage interest in space exploration and aerospace engineering.
  • Introduce spacecraft subsystems and their roles.
  • Demonstrate trade-offs between mass, cost, power, and mission capability.
  • Develop problem-solving and systems-thinking skills.
  • Provide an interactive educational experience for students and space enthusiasts.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of MISSION CONTROL is its combination of spacecraft construction, mission planning, resource management, and mission simulation in one interactive experience.

Instead of simply explaining spacecraft engineering, the game allows players to make interconnected decisions and see how those decisions influence a mission's outcome.

Technology and Tools

  • Godot 4 — Game engine
  • GDScript — Programming language
  • Blender or external 3D tools — Only if used for project assets
  • ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex — AI-assisted planning, documentation, coding, and debugging

The project is designed as a Windows desktop game.

Engineering Considerations

The game considers spacecraft mass, component cost, energy generation and consumption, communication capability, scientific instruments, launch vehicle capacity, and orbit selection.

These relationships are represented through simplified educational simulation models inspired by aerospace engineering concepts. The game is not intended to replace professional mission-design software or provide flight-certified engineering calculations.

Conclusion

MISSION CONTROL turns the challenge of designing a space mission into an accessible and interactive learning experience. It encourages players to think like mission designers, understand engineering trade-offs, and explore the possibilities of space exploration.
